product_backlog.title: List Management
product_backlog.description: Core data structures and list management features
Task creation, completion, and deletion features
product_backlog.title: Task Management
Create a new to-do list
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the home page, When they enter a list name and click create, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully create and view multiple named to-do lists.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified acceptance criteria for US-0001: User can create a new to-do list with a name and view it.

product_backlog.title: Add a task to a list
acceptance_criteria: Given a to-do list exists, When the user adds a task with a description, Then the task appears under that list.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can keep track of what needs to be done.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can add tasks with descriptions to their lists.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can keep track of what needs to be done.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified US-0002 acceptance criteria: Users can add tasks with descriptions to their lists.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can toggle task completion status and see visual distinction.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user marks the task as complete, Then its status changes to completed and it is visually distinguished.
product_backlog.title: Mark task complete or incomplete
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified acceptance criteria for US-0003: Users can mark tasks as complete or incomplete with visual distinction.

acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user deletes the task, Then the task is removed from the list.
product_backlog.title: Delete a task
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully remove unwanted tasks.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove items I no longer need.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove items I no longer need.
product_backlog.acceptance_check_note: Verified acceptance criteria for US-0004: Users can delete a task successfully.

product_backlog.title: Delete an entire list
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can delete lists along with their nested tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given a to-do list with tasks exists, When the user deletes the list, Then the list and all its associated tasks are removed.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up obsolete projects.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up obsolete projects.

acceptance_criteria: Given the user has created lists and tasks, When they view the main page, Then all lists and their tasks are displayed clearly, with completed tasks visually distinguished.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can view their lists and tasks overview with clear status differentiation.
product_backlog.title: View all lists and tasks
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to see all my lists and their tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I have a complete view of my work.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to see all my lists and their tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I have a complete view of my work.

Write pytest unit tests for list creation

risks_assumptions: Single process in-memory/SQLite storage is sufficient for MVP session persistence.
